facts.summary: Phase 2 trial missed primary and secondary endpoints; development ceased · Phase 2 · sabirnetug in early Alzheimer's disease · not yet approved

evidence.summary: the clinical trial did not meet its primary endpoint of change from baseline in cognitive and functional decline as measured by the Integrated Alzheimer’s Disease Rating Scale at 18 months compared to placebo
evidence.primary_endpoint_met: the clinical trial did not meet its primary endpoint of change from baseline in cognitive and functional decline as measured by the Integrated Alzheimer’s Disease Rating Scale at 18 months compared to placebo at either the 35 mg/kg or the 50 mg/kg dose
evidence.safety: The initial topline data indicate that sabirnetug was generally well tolerated, with amyloid-related imaging abnormalities - edema (“ARIA-E”) observed in ~10% of sabirnetug-treated participants.
evidence.program_discontinued: the Company plans to cease development of sabirnetug, including the open-label extension portion of the ALTITUDE-AD trial
